meals.name: Cuban mojo pork shoulder with garlicky black beans and rice
steps: Make the mojo: juice the orange and limes (about ½ cup) and whisk with 10 minced garlic cloves, ¼ cup olive oil, 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp oregano, 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper. Poke a 4 lb pork shoulder all over with a knife, rub in the mojo and marinate at least 2 hours or overnight.
Roast the pork with its marinade in a covered pan at 325°F for about 3½–4 hours, until fork-tender (well past 145°F, around 195°F for pulling). Uncover for the last 20 minutes to brown the top.
While it rests, cook 1½ cups rice. Soften ½ diced onion and 2 minced garlic cloves in 1 Tbsp oil, add the drained black beans, ½ tsp cumin and a splash of water and simmer 5 minutes.
Shred the pork, toss with a few spoonfuls of the pan juices and a squeeze of lime, and serve over rice with the beans.

meals.name: Korean-style sweet soy glazed chicken thighs with sesame broccoli
steps: Whisk the glaze: ⅓ cup soy sauce, 3 Tbsp brown sugar, 1 Tbsp honey, 1 Tbsp vinegar, 1 Tbsp sesame oil, 5 minced garlic cloves, 1 tsp ground ginger and ½ tsp red pepper flakes. Toss 3 lb bone-in chicken thighs in half of it and let sit 20 minutes.
Roast the thighs skin-side up on a foil-lined sheet at 425°F for 35–40 minutes, brushing with the remaining glaze for the last 10 minutes, until 165°F inside (175°F is even juicier).
Meanwhile cook 1½ cups rice. Cut 1½ lb broccoli into florets, toss with 1 Tbsp vegetable oil and a pinch of salt, and roast on a second sheet for the last 15 minutes.
Toss the hot broccoli with 1 tsp sesame oil and a splash of soy sauce. Serve the chicken over rice with the pan glaze spooned over and sliced green onions on top.

meals.name: Southern smothered pork chops in onion gravy with brown-butter sweet potatoes
steps: Peel and cube a 3 lb bag of sweet potatoes and boil 15 minutes until tender. Drain and mash with 2 Tbsp butter browned in a small pan, 1 Tbsp brown sugar and a pinch of salt.

Season 6 pork chops (about 2 lb) with 1 tsp each garlic powder and smoked paprika, salt and pepper, then dredge in ⅓ cup flour (save the extra). Brown in 1 Tbsp oil and 1 Tbsp butter in a large skillet, 3 minutes per side; set aside.
Add 1 more Tbsp butter and 1 large sliced onion to the pan and cook 8 minutes until golden. Stir in 2 Tbsp of the leftover flour, then whisk in 2 cups broth, 1 Tbsp Worcestershire and ½ tsp thyme.
Return the chops, cover and simmer on low 8–10 minutes until they reach 145°F and the gravy thickens. Serve the chops smothered in gravy with the sweet potatoes.

meals.name: Lemony garlic-butter shrimp scampi with linguine
steps: Cook 1 lb De Cecco linguine in well-salted water until al dente; save 1 cup pasta water before draining.

Pat 1½ lb peeled raw shrimp dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat 2 Tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high and cook the shrimp 1–2 minutes per side until pink and 145°F; move to a plate.
Lower the heat, add 4 Tbsp butter, 8 sliced garlic cloves and ½ tsp red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute. Add ½ cup broth or white wine, the zest and juice of the lemon, and simmer 2 minutes.
Toss in the pasta, shrimp, ¼ cup Parmesan and a splash of pasta water until glossy. Finish with chopped parsley and more lemon to taste.

meals.name: Smoky chili-lime chicken fajitas with charred peppers and onions
steps: Slice 2 lb chicken breast into strips. Toss with 2 Tbsp oil, the juice of 1 lime, 2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp each cumin, smoked paprika and garlic powder, ½ tsp oregano and 1 tsp salt. Marinate 15–30 minutes.
Heat a large skillet or cast-iron pan until very hot. Cook the chicken in batches without crowding, 5–6 minutes, until charred in spots and 165°F inside; set aside.

Add 1 Tbsp oil, 3 sliced bell peppers and 1 sliced onion to the pan with a pinch of salt and ½ tsp chili powder; cook 6–7 minutes until blistered but still crisp. Return the chicken and squeeze in the second lime.
Stir a few dashes of hot sauce and a pinch of lime zest into the sour cream. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan and pile in the fajitas with the spicy crema.

meals.name: Chipotle-roasted sweet potato and black bean tacos with avocado crema (meatless)
steps: Quick-pickle the onion: thinly slice the red onion and cover with ½ cup cider vinegar, ½ cup hot water, 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp salt. Let sit while you cook.

Peel 2 lb sweet potatoes, cut into ½-inch cubes and toss with 2 Tbsp olive oil, 2 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp each smoked paprika, cumin and garlic powder and 1 tsp salt. Roast at 425°F for 25–30 minutes, flipping once, until browned.
Warm the drained black beans in a small pot with a pinch of cumin, a squeeze of lime and a splash of water, mashing a few.
Blend or mash 2 avocados with ½ cup sour cream, the juice of 1 lime and a pinch of salt. Char the tortillas in a dry pan and fill with beans, sweet potatoes, crema and pickled onions.

meals.name: Cajun smoked sausage, peppers and tomato rice skillet
steps: Mix the Cajun seasoning: 2 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp each thyme, oregano and garlic powder, ½ tsp cayenne and ½ tsp black pepper.

Slice 2 smoked sausage ropes into coins and brown in 1 Tbsp oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven, 5 minutes; remove. Add 1 diced onion, 2 diced bell peppers, 2 diced celery ribs and 4 minced garlic cloves and cook 6 minutes.

Stir in the seasoning and 1½ cups rice for 1 minute, then add one 28 oz can of tomatoes, 2 cups broth, a bay leaf and the sausage. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat, then fluff, taste for salt, and finish with sliced green onions and hot sauce at the table.

meals.name: Crispy baked garlic-Parmesan wings with roasted vegetables
steps: Pat 4 lb whole wings very dry (split them into flats and drums if you like). Toss with 1 Tbsp baking powder, 2 tsp salt, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp smoked paprika and ½ tsp pepper.
Arrange on a rack set over a foil-lined sheet. Bake at 250°F for 30 minutes, then raise to 425°F and bake 40–45 minutes more, until crisp and at least 165°F inside.
For the last 25 minutes, roast the 32 oz bag of frozen vegetables on a second sheet with 1 Tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper.

Melt 4 Tbsp butter with 4 minced garlic cloves, ½ tsp red pepper flakes and 1 tsp dried parsley. Toss the hot wings in it with ½ cup finely grated Parmigiano and a squeeze of lemon; serve with the vegetables.

meals.name: Cider-mustard braised country-style ribs with apples and mashed potatoes
steps: Season 3 lb country-style ribs with 1 tsp smoked paprika, salt and pepper and brown well in 1 Tbsp oil in a Dutch oven, 3 minutes per side; set aside.
Add 1 sliced onion and 2 apples cut into wedges and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 3 minced garlic cloves, 2 Tbsp mustard, 2 Tbsp brown sugar, 2 Tbsp cider vinegar, 1 tsp thyme and 1½ cups broth.
Return the ribs, cover and braise at 325°F for 1½–2 hours until fork-tender (well past 145°F). Uncover and simmer the sauce on the stove a few minutes to thicken.
Meanwhile boil the peeled, cubed potatoes until tender and mash with 2 Tbsp butter, ½ cup warm milk and salt. Serve the ribs and apples over the mash with plenty of the tangy pan sauce.

meals.name: Birria-style beef tacos with dipping broth and avocado
steps: Brown 2½ lb birria-seasoned beef in chunks in 1 Tbsp oil in a Dutch oven. Add 1 chopped onion, 5 garlic cloves, one 14 oz can tomatoes, 3 cups broth, 1 Tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp each cumin and oregano, 2 bay leaves and 1 Tbsp vinegar.
Cover and simmer gently 2½–3 hours (or 3½ hours at 325°F in the oven) until the beef shreds easily. Shred the meat and season the broth with salt and a squeeze of lime.
Skim some of the red fat from the top of the broth. Dip each tortilla in it, lay in a hot skillet, top with cheese and beef, fold and crisp 2 minutes per side.
Serve the tacos with cups of the hot broth for dipping, sliced avocados, chopped onion, cilantro and lime wedges.
